title: Surge Hire Orbit Playbook and Mini Interview Lab
content:
Purpose: Quickplay hiring + onboarding framework for short-term surge hiring (3–8 hires in 6 weeks) when a product or reliability sprint needs capacity fast. Designed to be lightweight, repeatable, and evidence-forward so hiring decisions can be made asynchronously and onboarding gets hires to impact in 21 days.

Summary: Orbit Playbook organizes a 6-week timeline with three overlapping rhythms: source & funnel, interview lab (mini technical + behavioral), and compressed onboarding. This doc bundles the recruiter/manager checklist, an interview rubric template (compact, signal-focused), a one-page preboarding checklist, and a 21-day ramp map. Keep notes in the candidate evidence packet (link above) for committee review.

When to use:
- Emergency capacity requests from Eng/Product for critical launches or incidents.
- Short-term project pods where we can onboard to a scope-limited MLP.
- Hiring surges where time-to-offer needs to be measured in days not weeks.

Key principles (operational):
- Fail fast, document evidence: use a one-sheet candidate packet with 3 strongest signals and 1 risk.
- Standardize the mini-lab so each candidate sees the same stimulus and delivery window (3–6 hours).
- Prioritize ramp-to-impact: role scope must have a clearly scannable 30/60/90 for the pod.
- Use a single hiring committee template and asynchronous scoring to avoid meeting delays.

Roles & responsibilities (quick reference):
- Hiring Manager: defines sprint scope, finalizes job card, owns offer approval, designs mini-lab prompt.
- Recruiter: sources, screens for baseline fit, schedules interviews, maintains pipeline doc.
- People Ops Partner: coordinates compensation guardrails, offer templates, handles preboarding logistics.
- Interviewers: run structured mini-interview probes, submit rubric within 24 hours.
- Hiring Committee (3 people): reviews evidence packet, votes (yes/concerns/no) asynchronously within 48 hours.

Six-week timeline (compressed):
Week 0 (prep, 3–5 days):
- Hiring manager finalizes 3-sentence role purpose and 5 must-have signals.
- Recruiter posts quick job card, sources passive pipeline, prepares interviewers.
- Mini-lab prompt drafted and sanity-checked by one peer.

Week 1–3 (interview lab + offers):
- Screen (30m) -> Mini-lab (take-home or timed) -> Live deep-dive (60m)
- Target: move from screen to offer in 10 business days for prioritized candidates.
- Committee asynchronously reviews compiled evidence packet.

Week 4–6 (onboarding + stabilization):
- Preboarding completed, day0 kit and infra access granted, initial task assigned.
- Weekly sync with manager for first 3 weeks; ramp check at day 21.

Mini Interview Lab (template):
- Objective: measure actionable signals in 3 buckets: system reasoning, pragmatic debugging / prototype, team communication.
- Delivery window: 3–6 hours estimated, completed within 72 hours of assignment.
- Format: one short spec (200–400 words) + small data snippet or repo snippet + explicit success criteria.
- Example prompt (serving runtime candidate): "You have a model-serving flow that sees 30–40% request amplification when sequence length increases. Sketch a prioritized plan (3 actions) to reduce per-token cost while preserving 95th percentile latency SLOs. Provide expected tradeoffs and one pseudo-command or snippet you'd run to validate the top action."

Grading mini-lab:
- Use the compact rubric below. Interviewers should mark each field and add 1–2 lines of evidence. Keep it targeted.

Compact Interview Rubric (0–3 scale)
- Technical Signal (0–3): Right ideas for core problem, realistic tradeoffs.
- Execution Signal (0–3): Can break tasks into verifiable steps; shows pragmatic validation plan.
- Collaboration Signal (0–3): Communicates tradeoffs, flags unknowns, and proposes checkpoints.
- Culture / Craft fit (0–3): Ownership, documentation habits, and learning posture.
- Red flags (free text): plagiarism, evasive answers, major knowledge gaps.

Score interpretation (quick):
- 10–12: Strong hire. Evidence sheet should include 2x concrete artifacts (code snippet, design sketch).
- 7–9: Hire with conditions (mentor plan, explicit 30-day goals).
- <=6: Do not hire for surge scope.

Asynchronous committee flow:
- Within 24h of final interview, recruiter compiles: resume, screen notes, mini-lab, live-interview notes, rubric scores, 1-line recommended decision.
- Committee members annotate packet and vote within 48h. If split decision, the hiring manager calls a 15m tie-break.

Preboarding checklist (one-pager):
- Offer accepted -> send welcome + 1 pager: team scope, first task, buddy assigned.
- IT: request access: GitHub team, internal wiki, Cloud console (least privilege), infra sandbox.
- HR: paperwork form + payroll setup link, equity info, benefits packet.
- Manager: calendar blocks for first week (meet the team, 1:1, onboarding workshop).
- Buddy: intro message and 30-min synchronous walkthrough scheduled day0.

First 21-day ramp map (high-level tasks):
Day 0–3:
- Account access verification, dev environment boot, repo walk, run first end-to-end smoke (local or sandbox).
- Complete security basics training and SRE runbook reading.

Week 1 (day 4–7):
- Small bug or doc fix assigned that touches runtime path. Coach sits with them for the first PR.
- 1:1 with manager to align priority and define 30-day measurable.

Week 2 (day 8–14):
- Owner of a scoped ticket (bugfix/perf probe) and write-up of approach + results.
- Pairing session on deployment checklist and tracing tools.

Week 3 (day 15–21):
- Deliverable: ship scoped ticket and present 10-min postmortem of findings.
- Ramp review: manager + buddy + PO to sign off on day21 readiness.

Acceptance criteria for surge hires at day21:
- Pull request merged that touches serving/runtime path OR a complete operational runbook for assigned scope.
- Can explain three system-level tradeoffs that the team cares about.
- Has at least two positive peer feedback signals from pairing sessions.

Risk matrix & mitigations (common):
- Candidate lacks deep infra experience -> mitigation: allocate senior mentor and schedule weekly go/deep sessions.
- Onboarding friction from infra access delays -> mitigation: pre-request accounts on offer acceptance.
- Ramp overload due to chasing too many scopes -> mitigation: manager restricts first 3 weeks to single scoped ticket.

Templates (copy-and-paste friendly):
- 3-sentence role purpose: "Join the serving-runtime pod to reduce per-token cost and improve 95th percentile latency for inference workloads; own a scoped MLP with clear rollback and validation criteria."
- 5 must-have signals (comma-separated): production debugging experience, kernel/runtime profiling familiarity, practical latency SLO tradeoffs, clear asynchronous comms, ownership of a scoped shipping ticket.

Evidence capture fields (candidate packet):
- 3 strongest signals (1–2 lines each)
- 1 risk + proposed mitigation
- Mini-lab timestamp + delivery link
- Live interview notes (2–3 bullet highlights)
- Score breakdown (numbers and brief rationale)

Quick offer checklist:
- Salary band checked with People Ops, approval email from hiring manager, signatory name for offer.
- Draft offer letter, equity calc, start date negotiated, onboarding date pinned (preboarding begins on acceptance).

Retrospective prompts after surge cycle:
- What fraction of offers led to day21 acceptance criteria? (target >= 80%)
- Which mini-lab tasks correlated most with day21 impact?
- Where did pipeline sourcing break (quality/time)?

Notes to self (working):
- Keep mini-lab prompts small — aim for 1–2 evaluative moves not an architecture essay.
- Consider a dedicated surge interviewer pool for faster scheduling windows.
- Monitor candidate NPS on the process (quick 1-2 Qs) so we can iterate.

Questions / open items:
- Compensation guardrails for surge hires vs standard : who signs off on higher bands? (people ops)
- Should we compensate for the mini-lab in high-skill roles? (legal/comp to advise)
